prerequisites: Students must master specific mathematical and physical knowledge (statics, strength of materials, and structural calculation). It is recommended not to enroll without having successfully completed the courses: mechanics, strength of materials, and structural calculation.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Capacity for the clear and correct transmission of concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing.
Capacity for the use of scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for the search for sustainable engineering solutions.
Capacity for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

syllabus_topics: Elastic behavior: pure bending, simple bending, bending and axial load
Plastic behavior: tension/compression, pure bending, compound bending, skewed bending, simple bending
Resistance calculation: tension/compression, bending moment, bending and axial load, shear, bending and shear, bending, shear and axial load, torsion, torsion and bending
Buckling resistance: flexural buckling, torsional buckling, flexural-torsional buckling, lateral buckling
teaching_methods: Problem-based methodology with in-class problem-solving, concluding each topic with new exercise proposals for practical work to be reviewed in tutorials and/or seminars.
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 out of 10 points is required in each of the assessment components to pass the course.
